$about.purpose: Hand-authored template for The Wandering Pages. Scripted-survey-by-default: a railroad beat with an `options` array is rendered fully scripted (no AI call). Free text from the player still routes through the AI under CANON LOCK + BEAT GUIDANCE.
beat_modes: Fully scripted — beat has `description` + `options[]`. Description rendered verbatim, options used verbatim. No AI on preset picks.
Scripted scene, AI-tailored options — beat has `description` only. Description verbatim; AI generates 2-4 character-appropriate option labels.
No beat — AI improvises within tone/lore/restrictions.
Set `is_final: true` on a beat to end the journey at that scene.
supported_imports: Legacy survey graph — { surveyMeta, nodes[], edges[] }. Root ports become characters; BFS depth ≥ 2 nodes collapse into railroad beats, and their port labels populate each beat's scripted options automatically.
Wrapped exports — { adventure: {...} } or { config: {...} } are auto-unwrapped.
$about.off_track_resilience: When a player ignores the preset options and writes free text, the AI is told to (a) honor their action, (b) steer back toward the next railroad beat, and (c) only reference named entities that exist in `lore` below. Add a Story Bible entry for any person/place/thing you want the AI to be able to invoke.

restrictions: Stay PG-13. Never invent named NPCs, factions, or locations that aren't in the Story Bible. If the player asks about something off-canon, have an NPC redirect or plead ignorance rather than fabricating lore.

railroad_points.description: Write this verbatim — the player will read it as Scene 2. Stage the events, named NPCs from the Story Bible, and the reveal.

railroad_points.description: The final scene — render the climax exactly as written. Mark is_final so the journey ends here.

intro_node.description: Three travellers stand at the trailhead. Whose boots will you lace this morning?

options.label: Aria, the wandering scribe
options.recap: You are Aria — quill ink-stained, your satchel heavy with half-finished maps…
options.brief: Trained at the Vellum College; carries the only surviving rubbing of the Salt Chapel altarstone. Owes a debt to Mira the Lampwright.

options.label: Boran, the broken-oath knight
options.recap: You are Boran — a knight without a banner, sword nicked from a fight you lost on purpose…
options.brief: Discharged from the Lantern Guard after refusing a kill-order. Knows the lighthouse's lower passages from his garrison days.

lore.name: Mira the Lampwright
lore.body: Keeps the harbor lanterns. Gruff, fifties, missing two fingers. Secretly knows who drowned the previous keeper. Will trade information for lamp oil. Speaks in clipped sentences.

lore.name: Proctor Hesh
lore.body: Town magistrate. Officious, terrified of the chapel. Default authority figure the AI can deploy when a player goes somewhere unscripted and needs to be redirected with rules/warnings.

lore.name: The Lantern Guard
lore.body: Town's volunteer night watch. Boran was discharged from them. Will recognize him on sight.

lore.name: The Salt Chapel
lore.body: Half-collapsed shrine on the bluffs where smugglers leave offerings. Wet stone, gull bones, a single intact altarstone.

lore.name: The Drowned Lantern Inn
lore.body: Default safe location. Use this when a player wanders off-script and needs somewhere plausible to land — barkeep is a generic 'the innkeeper' unless you add one to the Bible.

lore.name: The lighthouse won't light
lore.body: Three years dark; the town blames the new keeper. This is the spine — most beats should bend back toward it.

lore.name: Mira drowned the old keeper
lore.body: Revealed only at beat 5 or later, or if the player directly accuses her with evidence. AI must NOT volunteer this.

lore.name: Off-track policy
lore.body: If the player goes somewhere with no beat and no Bible entry, have a known NPC (Proctor Hesh, Mira) intercept them and nudge back toward the lighthouse thread. Never name a new character.
